create.ponder.item_vault_storage.text_1: An Item Vault is a large container that holds far more items than a chest
create.ponder.item_vault_storage.text_2: It has no screen of its own: you cannot put items in or take them out by hand
create.ponder.item_vault_storage.text_3: Instead, item transport blocks such as chutes, funnels or belts fill it...
create.ponder.item_vault_storage.text_4: ...and can just as well empty it again
create.ponder.item_vault_sizes.text_1: Vaults placed against each other merge into one bigger vault with their combined space
create.ponder.item_vault_sizes.text_2: The square end of a vault may be at most 3 blocks across...
create.ponder.item_vault_sizes.text_3: ...and its length may reach three times that width
create.ponder.chute.text_1: A Chute carries items straight down, out of one inventory and into another
create.ponder.chute.text_2: Use a Wrench on a chute to give it a window
create.ponder.chute.text_3: Industrial Iron Blocks can be used to encase a chute
create.ponder.chute.text_4: A chute placed against the side of another one turns diagonal
create.ponder.chute_upward.text_1: With an Encased Fan at its top or bottom end, a Chute can lift items upward
create.ponder.chute_upward.text_2: Looking at a chute through Engineer's Goggles tells you which way it moves items
create.ponder.chute_upward.text_3: Items cannot leave through the end the fan is blocking, so inventories at the sides take them there
create.ponder.smart_chute.text_1: A Smart Chute is a vertical chute that comes with extra controls
create.ponder.smart_chute.text_2: Whatever item sits in its filter slot decides what it pulls out and lets through
create.ponder.smart_chute.text_3: Scroll on the value panel to choose how many items it takes in one go
create.ponder.smart_chute.text_4: While it is powered by redstone, a Smart Chute does nothing
create.ponder.brass_funnel.text_1: An Andesite Funnel only ever pulls out one item at a time
create.ponder.brass_funnel.text_2: A Brass Funnel can pull out up to a whole stack at once
create.ponder.brass_funnel.text_3: Its value panel lets you set exactly how many items one extraction takes
create.ponder.brass_funnel.text_4: Clicking its filter slot with an item makes the funnel move only that item
create.ponder.funnel_intro.text_1: Funnels are the easiest way to move items out of inventories and into them
create.ponder.funnel_direction.text_1: Placed the normal way, a funnel pulls items out of the inventory behind it
create.ponder.funnel_direction.text_2: Placed while sneaking, it puts items into the inventory instead
create.ponder.funnel_direction.text_3: A Wrench switches a funnel between the two modes after it has been placed
create.ponder.funnel_direction.text_4: The same rules hold on almost every side of a block
create.ponder.funnel_direction.text_5: On a belt, the belt's direction of travel decides whether the funnel inserts or extracts
create.ponder.funnel_compat.text_1: Funnels also cooperate with a number of other components
create.ponder.funnel_redstone.text_1: As long as it is powered by redstone, a funnel stops moving items
create.ponder.funnel_transfer.text_1: A funnel on its own can never move items from one closed inventory straight into another
create.ponder.funnel_transfer.text_2: For that job, a Chute or a Smart Chute is the better choice
create.ponder.funnel_transfer.text_3: The same goes for moving items sideways: put a Mechanical Belt in between
create.ponder.andesite_tunnel.text_1: Andesite Tunnels can be placed on belts to cover them up
create.ponder.andesite_tunnel.text_2: As soon as an Andesite Tunnel has belts leading away from its sides...
create.ponder.andesite_tunnel.text_3: ...it splits off exactly one item from every stack passing through
create.ponder.andesite_tunnel.text_4: The rest of the stack carries on along the belt
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_1: Brass Tunnels can be placed on belts to cover them up
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_2: Every open side of a Brass Tunnel has a filter slot of its own
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_3: A filter on the side items come in from turns back everything that doesn't match it
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_4: Filters on the sides items go out through sort them: matching items take that exit
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_5: If an item could leave through more than one side, the tunnel's distribution mode chooses where it goes
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_6: Brass Tunnels sitting on belts that run side by side join into one group
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_7: Items coming in are now shared out across every exit of the group
create.ponder.brass_tunnel.text_8: Items can also be put into a tunnel directly for this
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.header: Distribution Modes of the Brass Tunnel
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_1: How a Brass Tunnel hands out items can be adjusted
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_2: 'Split' tries to spread each stack evenly over the outputs that are free
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_3: An output that cannot accept any more items is left out
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_4: 'Forced Split' never leaves an output out: it waits until that output is free again
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_5: 'Round Robin' keeps stacks in one piece and hands them to the outputs in turn
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_6: Here too, an output that is full gets skipped
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_7: 'Forced Round Robin' never skips an output
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_8: 'Prefer Nearest' sends items to the outputs closest to where they came in
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_9: 'Randomize' gives whole stacks to outputs picked at random
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_10: 'Synchronize Inputs' is a setting only Brass Tunnels have
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_11: Items may only pass once every tunnel of the group has one waiting
create.ponder.brass_tunnel_modes.text_12: That way, all the belts involved deliver items at the same rate
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_1: A Mechanical Arm's inputs and outputs are chosen before the Arm is placed
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_2: Right-click a block while holding the Arm to make it a target
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_3: Right-click it again to switch between Input (blue) and Output (yellow)
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_4: Left-click a selected block to take it out of the selection
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_5: Once placed, the Arm works with the blocks you selected beforehand
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_6: It can have as many inputs and outputs as you like, as long as they are within reach
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_7: Not every kind of inventory can be handled by the Arm directly, though
create.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_8: Funnels and Depots can act as a go-between in such cases
create.ponder.mechanical_arm_filtering.h: Filtering Outputs of the Mechanical Arm
create.ponder.mechanical_arm_filtering.t: At times you will want the Arm to deliver only certain items to certain targets
The Mechanical Arm has no filter settings of its own
Brass Funnels used as targets, however, tell the Arm about their filter
The Arm won't pick up an item that none of its outputs would accept
create.ponder.mechanical_arm_modes.heade: Distribution modes of the Mechanical Arm
create.ponder.mechanical_arm_modes.text_: When there is more than one output an item could go to...
...the Arm decides based on its mode setting
The mode is set on its value panel
'Round Robin' simply goes through every available output in turn
An output that has no room left is skipped
'Forced Round Robin' never skips an output: it waits until there is room
'Prefer First' favours the outputs that were selected first when the Arm was set up
create.ponder.mechanical_arm_redstone.te: A Mechanical Arm that receives a redstone signal will not start a new cycle
It always completes the cycle it is already in the middle of first
So a short break in the signal makes it run exactly one cycle
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_1: Smart Observers can pick up on all sorts of events
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_2: It notices items or fluids stored in an ordinary container in front of it
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_3: Set its filter slot to watch for particular contents only
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_4: It also switches on when the block in front of it matches the filter
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_5: It can also keep an eye on belts, chutes and pipes in front of it...
create.ponder.smart_observer.text_6: ...and it gives off a pulse whenever an item goes into or out of a funnel
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_1: A Threshold Switch keeps watch over how full a container is
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_2: When the amount stored rises above the upper threshold...
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_3: ...the redstone output of the switch changes
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_4: It stays like that until the amount drops to the lower threshold
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_5: Feed that output to the supply, such as this Smart Chute, and the buffer always stays stocked
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_6: Its interface lets you change the two thresholds
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_7: With a filter, only matching items count towards the total
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_8: Fluid containers can be watched in much the same way...
create.ponder.threshold_switch.text_9: ...and, oddly enough, so can the length of a Rope Pulley's rope
create.ponder.portable_storage_interface: Inventories that ride on a moving contraption are hard to reach with automation
This component can work with that storage without the contraption having to stop
Place a second interface facing it, with a gap of 1 or 2 blocks between them
When they pass each other, the two interfaces connect
While they are connected, the stationary interface stands in for EVERY inventory on the contraption
Items can now be put in...
Once no items have moved for a while, the contraption continues on its way
A redstone signal stops the stationary interface from connecting
create.ponder.display_link.text_1: Display Links let you show live information on displays
create.ponder.display_link.text_2: Begin by right-clicking the display that should receive the text...
create.ponder.display_link.text_3: ...then place it against the block it should read from
create.ponder.display_link.text_4: Open its interface to choose and configure what gets sent
create.ponder.display_link.text_5: From now on, the display is kept up to date by the link
create.ponder.display_link.text_6: Not every block can serve as a source
create.ponder.display_link.text_7: Each supported block has its own kinds of information to offer
create.ponder.display_link.text_8: A Display Link can write to several different kinds of display
create.ponder.display_link_redstone.head: Redstone Control
create.ponder.display_link_redstone.text: A Display Link that is powered by redstone stops sending updates
When the signal goes away, its timer restarts and new information is sent at once
Redstone power that reaches only the source block has no effect on the link
create.ponder.display_board.text_1: Display Boards are a sign that can be built as large as you need
create.ponder.display_board.text_2: They need rotational force to work
create.ponder.display_board.text_3: Click them with a written Clipboard to put up fixed text
create.ponder.display_board.text_4: Text that changes over time comes from a Display Link
create.ponder.display_board.text_5: Each line of the board can be coloured with dye on its own
create.ponder.display_board.text_6: Click a line with an empty hand to clear it
